`SIGTERM` can interrupt `Event.wait` while the environment server holds its condition lock. The current signal handler calls `Event.set`, which requires the same lock. The official CLI then cannot stop or close its active world.

This PR targets `feat/sim-policy-separation`, the branch for #4888. The diff contains only this shutdown fix and its regression tests.

## Related issues

Related: #4888.

## What changed

The signal handler sets a Boolean flag. The server owner reads that flag through an optional stop predicate and closes its resources normally. Other threads continue to use `server.stop.set()`. The CLI restores the previous `SIGTERM` handler before it returns.

## How was this tested (or how to run locally)

The regression starts the official CLI module with a Toy configuration. A real client opens a world and completes a step. A trace then selects signal delivery while `Event.wait` holds its lock. The test leaves `Event.wait` and the CLI handler unchanged.

The unchanged source deadlocks under controlled `SIGTERM` and requires `SIGKILL` after five seconds. The fixed source exits normally. Four CLI cases cover `SIGTERM` and `SIGINT`, with normal and controlled delivery. They check backend closure and handler restoration.

Ten focused tests pass. The complete `tests/env_server` directory also passes: 49 tests with process exit zero. An audited repeat verifies that all 352 loaded LeRobot modules come from the fixed checkout. Both full directory runs use `--confcutdir=tests/env_server`, which excludes unrelated root fixtures. All applicable changed-file `pre-commit` hooks pass, including project-wide mypy. Ten normal `SIGTERM` trials pass on each source version. The repository-wide test suite is not verified.

```sh
pytest --confcutdir=tests/env_server tests/env_server -q
```

- [x] Applicable changed-file formatting, lint, security, and mypy checks pass.
- [x] Focused tests pass locally.
- [ ] Full test suite passes locally.
- [ ] CI is green.
- [x] Community Review: [review of #4865](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/pull/4865#pullrequestreview-5459937609).

"**TL;DR:** on one H200, 86% of a bf16 pi0.5 chunk (133 of 154 ms) is the 10 denoise steps, which look launch-bound: `compile_model` brings the chunk to 25 ms but takes 3 to 7 minutes to warm up. Proposal: keep the prefix KV static per chunk and add an opt-in CUDA graph for the denoise step, to get most of that speedup without the compile warmup (draft PR in progress).

### Ticket Type

💡 Feature Request / Improvement

### Environment & System Info

- lerobot `main` 38b975c5b, `lerobot/pi05_base` @ 22c30e5b
- 1x H200, torch 2.11.0+cu128, transformers 5.5.4, `uv sync --locked --extra pi`

### Description

I profiled `PI05Pytorch.sample_actions` on one H200 to see where a chunk's time goes. Inputs are synthetic but shaped like `pi05_base`: 3 cameras at 224x224, 200 prompt slots (64 unmasked), chunk 50, 10 denoise steps, fixed noise. Each setting ran in its own process, 50 timed calls after 5 warmup; the first four rows ran twice in opposite order, the follow-ups once. Weights were checked tensor by tensor against the checkpoint.

| batch 1 | median ms per chunk (2 runs) | vs as shipped | first call | max abs diff vs fp32 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fp32 (as shipped) | 237 / 239 | 1.0x | 0.5 s | 0 |
| fp32 + `set_float32_matmul_precision("high")` | 148 / 149 | 1.6x | 0.4 s | 0.0003 |
| bf16 | 151 / 156 | 1.55x | 0.8 s | 0.011 |
| bf16 + `compile_model` (max-autotune) | 25.5 / 25.3 | 9.4x | 389 s cold, 46 s warm cache | 0.006 |
| bf16 + compile `reduce-overhead` (1 run) | 27.6 | 8.6x | 219 s | 0.014 vs bf16 |
| bf16 + compile `default` (1 run) | 44.2 | 5.4x | 188 s | 0.014 vs bf16 |

Where the bf16 eager time goes (CUDA events around each stage, separate runs): vision + embed 9.8 ms, prefix 12.0 ms, **10 denoise steps 133 ms** (in fp32 as shipped the prefix is 92 ms and the denoise steps 124 ms).

The charts also show the draft PR's CUDA-graph denoise (same H200 and inputs; its actions are `torch.equal` to the eager path's).

![Stacked bars, ms per chunk on one H200 at batch 1: fp32 as shipped 238 ms (vision 23, prefix 92, denoise 124); fp32 + TF32 148 ms; bf16 154 ms (vision 10, prefix 12, denoise 130); bf16 with the draft PR's CUDA-graph denoise 56 ms; compile reduce-overhead 28 ms and max-autotune 25 ms, not split by stage.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/arun-elr/lerobot/2b774306d82687153852726aa8af55ff4e0d6b5b/issue5148/pi05_stages_h200.png)

What that suggests:

1. **The denoise loop looks launch-bound.** Each extra denoise iteration (the step plus its Euler update) adds about 1,163 GPU ops in the profiler (10 steps minus 1 step, divided by 9), at about 13 ms per step for the `gemma_300m` expert on a 50-token suffix. Inductor alone (`default`) brings the whole chunk to 44 ms; adding CUDA graphs (`reduce-overhead`) brings it to 27.6 ms, within 9% of max-autotune.
2. **Every step copies the prefix cache.** The forward appends the suffix K/V into whatever `DynamicCache` it is given (HF Gemma updates it even with `use_cache=False`), so `denoise_step` clones the 968-token prefix cache each step and the clone grows to 1,018. Without the clone, step 2 sees 1,068 keys against a 1,018-wide mask: `The size of tensor a (1068) must match the size of tensor b (1018)`. It's the same pattern #4633 reports for SmolVLA, with a fix proposed in #4634.
3. **Compile's startup is the catch:** the first call took 188 to 420 s on a cold Inductor cache (46 s with a warm one), on top of loading the model, and a fresh machine or container pays it before its first action (#4115 is a related warmup crash in rollout).
4. **Compile at larger batch crashes:** `compile_model` at batch 8 (and with Gemma attention switched to `pi_gemma.sdpa_attention_forward`, already at batch 4) dies with `CUDA driver error: an illegal memory access`, reported at a fused cat/cumsum kernel over the 968-token prefix. Batch 4 with plain compile works (59 ms for 4 chunks), and eager bf16 at batch 8 works (240 ms).

![Scatter of steady-state ms per chunk against first-call time on a log scale: eager fp32 238 ms and bf16 154 ms start in under a second; the draft PR's CUDA graph is 56 ms with a 0.8 s first call; compile is 25 to 44 ms but its first call takes 188 to 389 s on a cold cache, 46 s warm.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/arun-elr/lerobot/2b774306d82687153852726aa8af55ff4e0d6b5b/issue5148/pi05_latency_vs_startup_h200.png)

![Grouped bars of action chunks per second at batch 1, 4 and 8: bf16 eager 7, 21, 33; with the draft PR's CUDA graph 18, 38, 46; compile max-autotune 39, 68, and a crash (illegal memory access) at batch 8.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/arun-elr/lerobot/2b774306d82687153852726aa8af55ff4e0d6b5b/issue5148/pi05_batch_throughput_h200.png)

### Context & Reproduction

Proposal, in the spirit of #4634 and #2061:

- keep the prefix K/V static once per chunk (concatenate the suffix functionally, no in-place growth, no per-step clone), and build the suffix masks and position ids once per chunk instead of every step;
- then an opt-in that captures `denoise_step` in a CUDA graph (fixed shapes per batch size and `chunk_size`), so the loop replays without `torch.compile`'s startup.

Before writing it I'd measure graph capture of the eager step on its own, since the 27.6 ms above also includes Inductor's fusion. Does this direction sound right, and is anyone already on it? Happy to open the PR.

<details><summary>How it was measured</summary>

- `sample_actions(images, img_masks, tokens, masks, noise=noise, num_steps=10)` under `torch.inference_mode()`, wall time with `torch.cuda.synchronize()`; stage times with CUDA events in separate runs so the wrappers don't touch the totals.
- bf16 arms all run at matmul precision `"high"`, the setting `compile_model` switches on, so compile isn't credited with TF32.
- "max abs diff" compares the 50x32 action chunk with the fp32 run on the same noise (the follow-up rows with bf16).
- Memory (steady state, `max_memory_allocated`): fp32 15.8 GiB, bf16 8.9 GiB, compiled 8.7 GiB.
</details>

### Relevant logs or stack trace

```
RuntimeError: CUDA driver error: an illegal memory access was encountered
  ... torch/_inductor/cudagraph_trees.py ... run_eager
  ... triton_spl_fused__to_copy_cat_cumsum_expand_sub_unsqueeze_22.run(..., 4, 968, ...)
```
(batch 4 with SDPA attention; batch 8 plain compile fails the same way)

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing tickets to ensure this isn't a duplicate.
- [x] I am using the latest version of the `main` branch.
- [ ] I have verified this is not an environment-specific problem.

### Additional Info / Workarounds

For anyone hitting the latency today: `dtype: bfloat16` plus `torch.set_float32_matmul_precision("high")` is ~1.55x with no compile warmup; `compile_model` is ~9x if a few minutes of first-call compile is acceptable.

**Offline: 2.1x faster pi0.5 inference on one L4**, from 0.31 s to 0.15 s per action chunk. Simulation: the ten-step teacher and readout each succeeded on 8/8 paired LIBERO-Long episodes.

Add an opt-in, shared readout for **pi0, pi0.5, SmolVLA and FineART-VLA**. `gaussian_readout_path=None` preserves each existing sampler. A fitted artifact selects one frozen action-network pass followed by Gaussian motion and binary gripper sampling. Teacher and processor hashes must match. No checkpoint conversion or new dependency is included.

Based on [Gaussian Distillation of Flow Policies](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.40271) by Saied, Sheebaelhamd, Vernade and Fleuret. This is an independent implementation; the paper says its code will be released soon.

Fixes https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/issues/5173.

## Evidence

Offline timing: [completed L4 job](https://huggingface.co/jobs/hadriencornier/6ae5343e0e0338d1bb7cfb64), checkpoint `lerobot/pi05_libero_finetuned_v044`, 8 held-out contexts and 160 samples per path.

| Path | Median | p95 | Speed vs ten-step teacher |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Ten-step teacher | 0.31 s | 0.32 s | 1.0x |
| Gaussian readout | 0.15 s | 0.15 s | **2.1x** |
| Raw one-step teacher, timing diagnostic | 0.15 s | 0.15 s | 2.1x |

Offline held-out mean MSE: **0.014**. Simulation: one LIBERO-Long basket task, 16 paired episodes, teacher **8/8**, readout **8/8**. Both used only the soup-then-sauce order; the two-order check is inconclusive.

### Why not just one Euler step?

For an ideal flow field, one full Euler step returns the conditional mean, which can lie between incompatible actions. The readout instead fits the **multistep teacher's mean and variance**, then samples them in one pass. Our raw one-step measurement covers timing only; no one-step quality advantage is claimed.

The Gaussian replaces the **whole sampler**, not only the last solver step. At a fixed context it is unimodal. The paper shows trajectory diversity through repeated stochastic actions and state feedback, not preservation of arbitrary conditional action modes ([sections 4.2 and 5.4](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.40271v1#S5.SS4)). Our proof does not establish mode preservation.

The mixed Gaussian/Bernoulli policy has an explicit likelihood. `log_prob` scores normalized chunks before clipping/postprocessing. This may enable likelihood-based fine-tuning such as PPO or GRPO; neither is implemented or demonstrated here.

## Scope and follow-ups

pi0, pi0.5, SmolVLA and eager FineART-VLA share a Linear velocity projection, so each needs only a feature helper and default-off dispatch. Other upstream flow policies also qualify in principle, but require separate adapters:

| Follow-up policies | Why separate work |
| --- | --- |
| GR00T N1.7, Evo-1, LaWAM | Embodiment-specific/nonlinear decoders and action masks; different time/probe conventions, including Evo-1's uniform noise. The paper evaluated GR00T N1.5. |
| EO-1, DM0.5, LingBot-VLA v2, Wall-X, Wall-OSS-0.5, MolmoAct2 | Different action-token layouts, masked dimensions, cache/position interfaces or conditioned output heads. |
| MultiTaskDiT, VLA-JEPA | Different objective/decoder contracts and noise-at-zero schedules; MultiTaskDiT also supports DDPM and residual-noise flow objectives. |
| Fast-WAM, Long-WAM, LingBot-VA, FLUX.3 | Video/action sampling, guidance and stream-specific caches/schedulers require a separately defined action marginal. |

## Validation and reproduction

CPU random-weight tests fit and sample each supported policy using tiny attention backbones; they check frozen teacher weights, one action-feature pass, artifact validation, RNG isolation and likelihoods. A separate comparison against upstream `main` checked byte-identical default outputs and RNG states for all four policies with generated/supplied noise and different step counts.

The original experiment runner remains [pinned in the proof commit](https://github.com/Hadrien-Cornier/lerobot/blob/973b159ad2c20aaddba9983abef59dc3d845361f/experiments/gar/proof.py). It is excluded from the final diff to keep simulator setup and experiment orchestration out of the library change.

## Limits

One checkpoint, one GPU and one simulated task; no real-arm result or raw one-step quality ablation. Added policies have CPU plumbing proofs only. Artifacts currently support continuous motion plus one binary gripper. The readout rejects RTC, memory modes, explicit starting noise/step counts and compiled/fused backends.
